keyframe_review.note: UNVERIFIED start: no page opened dates the judicate before the 11th century. The Arborea infobox says 'Established in the 11th century'; the Judicates page has Pope John VIII calling the Sardinian rulers principes Sardiniae in 872 and the 'first incontrovertible source' for four kingdoms on 14 October 1073 (judges Orzocco of Cagliari, Orzocco d'Arborea, Marianus of Torres, Constantine of Gallura). Shape left as Cliopatria draws it (3,878 km2, Oristano and the Campidano); no infobox area to compare.
Same unverified status as 866; Marianus I (1060-1070) is the first dated judge on the Arborea page.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1015 shape, valid 1015 to May 1016; the 1018 shape applies from May 1016

keyframe_review.note: Mujahid of Denia 'landed with 120 ships and occupied the southern coastal plain' in 1015 and in 1016 'defeated the army of the judge of Cagliari'; in May 1016 he 'fled by sea'. The page names no Arborean land, so the loss of four south-western cells is Cliopatria's; the withdrawal in May 1016 means the shape should end in 1016, not 1017.

correction.text: Arborea alone, as in the 1072 shape

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria joins Arborea to Logudoro (12,248 km2) for 1066-1071. The pages name separate judges: Marianus I 1060-1070 and Orzocorre I from 1070 in Arborea; Barisone I of Torres '1060-1073' in Logudoro; and on 14 October 1073 Gregory VII's letter names Orzocco d'Arborea and Marianus of Torres as different judges. (The Logudoro page says the two were 'combined at the start of the 11th century' and that 'On the death of Barisone I, Arborea chose its own judge in Marianus de Zori', which would support a union to 1073; the pages disagree, so the union is not used.)

The 3,855 km2 core of 250 years. The pages say Cagliari 'was conquered by a Pisan-Sardinian alliance in 1258' and its territory 'divided among the victors', and that Logudoro after 1259 'was effectively ruled by the Genoese families of Doria and Malaspina, and the ruling family of Arborea'; neither names the land Arborea took, so no correction is drawn: unverified: page budget.

+290 km2 (three cells) from 1326. Hugh II became a vassal of James II of Aragon on 11 April 1323 and the Aragonese took the Pisan lands (Cagliari, Gallura) by 1326, but the page names no Arborean gain; left as drawn: unverified.

Valid 1344-1367. 'In 1368 an Arborean offensive succeeded in nearly driving out the Aragonese from the island', reducing the Kingdom of Sardinia to Cagliari and Alghero; Marianus IV broke the alliance in 1353 (no territorial result given).

The Aragonese kept Cagliari and Alghero in 1368 and 'A peace treaty returned the Aragonese their previous possessions in 1388'; in 1391 Brancaleone Doria 'swept most of the island into Arborean rule'; Oristano fell in March 1410. Use the island less Cagliari and Alghero for 1375-1387 and 1391-1409.

New keyframe 1410-1420: 'Oristano fell in March 1410 without resistance' and Leonard Cubell was given the Marquisate of Oristano and County of Goceano; the infobox gives the capital as Sassari 1410-1420, and the kingdom 'ceased to exist in 1420'. Cliopatria draws the whole island to 1421 (26,138 km2). Oristano and the south went to Cubell's marquisate in 1410; the Judicate was 'disestablished August 14, 1420' (infobox) and 'ceased to exist in 1420' (Judicates page). Use the Sassari remnant of the previous keyframe.

region.text: Pisan Sardinia: Villa di Chiesa (Iglesias) and the former judicate of Cagliari

ledger.note: 1323: Arborea and Aragon against Pisa. On 11 April 1323 Hugh II 'became vassal of James II in exchange for maintenance of the dynastic rights over his Judicate' and 'opened hostilities against the Pisans'; on 28 June the Aragonese besieged Villa di Chiesa 'at the request of the Judge of Arborea'.

June 1326: Pisa's last Sardinian stronghold goes. 'Castel di Castro passed to the newborn Kingdom of Sardinia in June 1326' (capital of the new kingdom); Villa di Chiesa fell on 7 February 1324 and Pisa gave up Cagliari and Gallura on 29 February 1324.

wars.outcome: Mujahid landed in 1015, returned in 1016 and defeated the army of the judge of Cagliari, but was driven out in May 1016 by mutiny and the Pisan and Genoese fleets.
wars.note: The page names Cagliari only; Arborea's part is Cliopatria's (all four Sardinian shapes shrink in 1015-1017).

wars.name: Aragonese conquest of Sardinia

zones.text: Villa di Chiesa and the Pisan judicates of Cagliari and Gallura

wars.outcome: Villa di Chiesa surrendered on 7 February 1324, Pisa gave up Cagliari and Gallura on 29 February 1324 keeping Castel di Castro, which passed to the Kingdom of Sardinia in June 1326; Arborea was Aragon's vassal and ally.
wars.note: Hugh II became James II's vassal on 11 April 1323.

wars.name: Arborean-Aragonese wars
wars.outcome: Marianus IV broke the alliance in 1353; the 1368 offensive left the Aragonese Cagliari and Alghero; the 1388 peace returned their possessions; Brancaleone Doria swept most of the island again in 1391; Arborea lost at Sanluri on 30 June 1409 and Oristano fell in March 1410.
wars.note: The Arborea page dates the Battle of Sanluri to 30 June 1409 against William III of Narbonne. The Aragonese-conquest page gives no detail for 1353-1367.

certainty.note: The judicate was divided into 13 or 14 curatoriae but its external frontiers with Cagliari, Logudoro, Gallura and the Aragonese were never delimited on the pages opened; the sea is the only firm edge.

notes: Page budget (5) used. No page gives an infobox area, so the area comparison could not be made; the Cliopatria island shape (26,138 km2) is the whole of Sardinia (83 of 84 cells). Start: unverified. The Arborea infobox says 'Established in the 11th century' and the Judicates page has no date for the division into four judicates (first incontrovertible source 14 October 1073); Cliopatria starts the four Sardinian judicates in 866 and the dossier keeps that year at confidence 1, with the 866-1065 shapes kept unverified. The same call applies to Cagliari, Gallura and Logudoro, written by other agents. Cliopatria rows to correct: 1066-1071 joins Arborea to Logudoro, which the Arborea and Judicates pages contradict (separate judges); 1375-1421 draws the whole island, including Cagliari and Alghero, while the Aragonese kept them in 1368 and the Judicate was reduced to a Sassari remnant after March 1410 and ended in August 1420. Vassalage: Hugh II became James II's vassal on 11 April 1323 (Aragonese conquest page); under the schema the Crown of Aragon dossier should carry a vassal_start in 1323 (counterpart giudicato-of-arborea) and a vassal_end in 1353, when Marianus IV broke the alliance. Not drawn for lack of land on the pages: Arborea's share of Cagliari's territory in 1258 and of Logudoro after 1259; Barison's 1164 coronation as King of Sardinia (revoked the next year); the 1192 Treaty of Oristano. Gazetteer: Alghero, Tharros, Castelsardo and Sanluri are missing; Oristano is spelled 'Oristrano' in admin1; Iglesias exists only as the province Carbonia-Iglesias. Rulers omitted: only scattered reigns on the pages (Marianus I 1060-1070, Hugh II 1321-1336, Marianus IV 1353-1375 or 1347-1376, Eleanor 1387-1404, Marianus V d. 1407).
